title: Detect Before You Disambiguate: Perturbation-Based Input Ambiguity Detection in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.36353v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often answer ambiguous inputs as if they had a single intended meaning. This is problematic because input ambiguity is an upstream source of uncertainty: when a prompt admits multiple valid interpretations, the key question is whether the model should answer directly at all. Existing input uncertainty methods often rely on LLM-generated statements or clarifications, but such transformations may already disambiguate the input before the ambiguity is measured. We propose a label-preserving perturbation framework for input ambiguity detection in which perturbations remain close to the original input while preserving its label. We instantiate this principle with two detectors: a black-box rule-based perturbation library and a white-box importance-guided method using model-internal signals. translated_title: 先检测再消歧：基于扰动的LLM输入歧义检测
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）常常将含糊的输入当作只有单一意图的含义来回答。这是有问题的，因为输入歧义是不确定性的上游来源：当一个提示存在多种有效解释时，关键问题是模型是否应该直接回答。现有的输入不确定性方法通常依赖于LLM生成的陈述或澄清，但这种转换可能在测量歧义之前就已经对输入进行了消歧。我们提出了一个保持标签的扰动框架用于输入歧义检测，其中扰动在保持接近原始输入的同时保留其标签。我们用两种检测器实例化这一原则：一种基于规则的黑盒扰动库，以及一种利用模型内部信号的白盒重要性引导方法。在开放域、对话式和视觉问答领域的四个数据集上的实验表明，我们的方法优于输出侧不确定性方法。
tldr: 本文提出一种保持标签的扰动框架，通过黑盒规则扰动和白盒重要性引导两种检测器，在LLM对输入消歧之前检测输入歧义，在开放域、对话和视觉问答数据集上均优于现有的输出侧不确定性方法。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a label-preserving perturbation framework for detecting input ambiguity in LLMs before disambiguation, instantiated with a black-box rule-based perturbation library and a white-box importance-guided detector, outperforming output-side uncertainty methods across open-domain, conversational, and visual QA datasets.
